clue.text: Holding ears misinterpreted what doctor may have put into words

indicators.note: holding means the doctor's letters wrap round the scrambled ears

parts.note: a doctor may hold a PhD, a doctorate

indicators.note: misinterpreted tells us the letters of ears are read in a different order

explanation.surface: A doctor puts into words a misheard remark while cupping someone's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' looks like gripping someone's ears, but it signals a container; 'misinterpreted' is the anagram signal, and 'what doctor may have' points to a qualification, not a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To phrase something is to express it in words, so phrased means expressed verbally.

clue.text: Pretentious-sounding bunch

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for pretentious is heard, not spelt

parts.note: posey means pretentious, showing off

explanation.surface: A showy bouquet seems a bit pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bunch of flowers.

clue.text: Welcome back after the break?

parts.note: reads like a host's greeting after an advert break, but means letting someone in again, perhaps after a prison break

explanation.definitionFit: To readmit is to let someone in again, welcoming them back.

clue.text: Bargain offer, to get married in holy city

parts.note: a sale offers bargains

explanation.surface: A couple seize a discount deal to wed in a sacred city.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem is an old name for Jerusalem, the holy city, in Genesis and the Psalms.

clue.text: Approach tense listener

parts.note: drawn means tense, strained
an ear is a listener

explanation.surface: Someone moves towards a nervous person who is listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw near is to come closer, to approach.

clue.text: Make to go further in sort of limousine

definitions.meaning: make a resource last or extend longer

explanation.surface: Someone extends a ride in a long luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch a supply is to make it last longer; a stretch limo is an elongated limousine.

clue.text: Car's appeal to idiot

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crosswordese for appeal
a loon is a fool

explanation.surface: A car's attraction is to a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Car's means is, a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a British car with a separate boot, called a sedan in America.

clue.text: Roughest criminal one imprisoned, just

indicators.note: imprisoned means the one is locked inside the rearranged letters
criminal suggests the letters of roughest are bent into another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The roughest criminal has been jailed, and justly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges ROUGHEST, and 'imprisoned' locks I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright, just.

clue.text: Millions are put off fried food

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad and shifted out of order

explanation.surface: Millions of people are put off greasy fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges M plus ARE PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is Japanese battered and deep-fried seafood or vegetables.

clue.text: Man with capital M accepts one old religion

parts.note: he refers to a man

indicators.note: accepts means the group of pieces takes in the one

parts.note: Athens is the capital of Greece
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man with a capital M takes on an ancient faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man with capital M' looks like emphasis on a capital letter; it is HE with ATHENS and M, which 'accepts' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenism is paganism, an old belief system outside the major faiths.

clue.text: Slow delivery of armour to one being shelled

parts.note: a snail is a creature that carries a shell
mail is chain armour

explanation.surface: A suit of armour is delivered to a creature under attack by shellfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled' suggests bombardment, but it means having a shell, as a snail does.
explanation.definitionFit: Snail mail is a jokey name for the ordinary postal service, slower than email.

clue.text: African country where I left old instrument

indicators.note: left means the letter I has departed from the country's name

parts.note: Gambia is a West African country

explanation.surface: In a certain African country, someone abandoned an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The gamba, short for viola da gamba, is an early bowed stringed instrument, now largely historical.

clue.text: Crisis time spin-doctor aims to avoid?

definitions.meaning: a decisive moment when things are put to the test
a spin-doctor's job is to keep the plain facts from coming out, playfully read as avoiding the instant of honesty

explanation.surface: A political press officer tries to dodge a crucial moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive testing moment is called this; a spin-doctor naturally avoids honesty being revealed.

clue.text: Conversations have value in house

parts.note: chats are conversations
worth is value

explanation.surface: Talks are worthwhile inside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: CHATSWORTH is a famous stately home in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatsworth House is a grand English country house, seat of the Dukes of Devonshire.

clue.text: Anne has gone

parts.note: hath is the old form of has
away means gone, absent

explanation.surface: Someone called Anne has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne looks like the subject of a sentence; it defines Shakespeare's wife's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Hathaway was Shakespeare's wife, and is also a modern actress, so the name completes Anne.

clue.text: Acton governess wastes energy (gas)

indicators.note: wastes suggests the letters are squandered and scattered

explanation.surface: A governess in Acton squanders energy by leaving the gas on.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton Bell was Anne Brontë's pen name; her novel's heroine is a governess. Acton looks like the London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes Grey is the title heroine of Anne Brontë's novel, published as by Acton Bell.

clue.text: Hunter runs out, returning across a field

indicators.note: across means the turned letters stretch either side of the a
returning means the shortened hunter's name is read backwards
out tells us the letter for runs is dropped from the hunter

parts.note: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A hunter dashes out and comes back over a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops R from NIMROD to leave NIMOD; 'returning' turns it into DOMIN, which goes across A.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a field of activity or knowledge, a sphere of interest.

clue.text: Magistrate took risk with execution — shabby

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice

indicators.note: execution means beheading, removing the first letter

parts.note: dared means took a risk

explanation.surface: A magistrate gambled and was executed, all looking threadbare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with execution' beheads DARED to leave ARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-eared describes pages worn and turned down at the corners, hence shabby.

clue.text: Turandot's gracious words to minister for providing recording?

parts.note: ta is informal British thanks, a polite expression
Ping is one of the three ministers in Puccini's opera Turandot

explanation.surface: Princess Turandot offers a courteous thank-you to one of her court officials.
explanation.walkthrough: Turandot's points to the opera, whose three ministers are Ping, Pang and Pong.
explanation.definitionFit: Taping is making a recording on tape, so it means providing a recording.

clue.text: At last slip on a seaweed — bother!

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of slip is taken

parts.note: laver is an edible seaweed

explanation.surface: Someone finally slips on some seaweed and swears.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver means fuss and bother, a needless to-do.

clue.text: Grain cost us double? No way at all!

indicators.note: double means the shortened phrase is written twice
No tells us the letters for way are removed from cost us

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone protests that the grain will cost twice as much, refusing outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' with 'way at all' removes ST from COSTUS to leave COUS, which 'double' writes twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is a North African food made from granules of semolina, a grain product.

clue.text: Old scene of mutiny kept quiet, away from the sea

indicators.note: kept means the sandbank holds the quiet inside it

parts.note: the Nore, a Thames estuary anchorage, saw a naval mutiny in 1797
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: An old mutiny site was hushed up, far from the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nore is a sandbank anchorage in the Thames estuary where the Royal Navy mutinied in 1797; 'kept' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Onshore means on land, away from the sea.

clue.text: PC is fit, in trim

indicators.note: in means the fitting word goes inside the trimming word

parts.note: to lop is to trim
apt means fit, suitable

explanation.surface: A computer is in good shape and trim.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like police constable; it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer.

clue.text: No one has a beard, note, during fighting —- keep it to yourself!

indicators.note: during means the clean-shaven phrase and note sit inside the fighting

parts.note: wars are fighting
if no one has a beard, all shave
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: During a battle, every soldier is clean-shaven, and someone urges secrecy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places ALL SHAVE plus E inside WARS.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying warns that someone may be eavesdropping, so stay discreet and say nothing.

clue.text: Noble lion? Almost crooked

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: aslant means crooked, slanting

explanation.surface: A noble lion is nearly bent out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslan is the noble lion of C S Lewis's Narnia books.

clue.text: Disobey God: fine for it

indicators.note: for means the letter for fine takes the place of it

parts.note: a deity is a god
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone disobeys God and is fined for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps IT in DEITY for F.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy is to openly disobey.

clue.text: Current holder of licence doesn't get started

indicators.note: the first letter of the licence holder is dropped

parts.note: a driver holds a driving licence

explanation.surface: The present licence holder fails to begin something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't get started' removes D from DRIVER. 'Current' reads as an adjective meaning present, but is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flowing current of water through the land.

clue.text: Give free rein to lust, or one explodes

indicators.note: explodes means the letters of lust, or one are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lets their desire run wild, or else bursts out.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something loose is to release it, letting it go unrestrained.

clue.text: Run into Ben — yes, run!

indicators.note: into means the letter for run is placed inside the name

parts.note: Hur follows Ben in the title of the film Ben-Hur
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
yup is informal yes

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into Ben, who says yes and tells them to dash.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben stands for its partner HUR, as in Ben-Hur.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry up is an urgent command to go faster, much like run.

clue.text: Refuse to accept own interests being curtailed in a crowd

indicators.note: to accept means the refusal wraps round the shortened self

parts.note: to refuse is to deny

indicators.note: being curtailed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: self, as in self-interest, means one's own interests

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to let their own interests be reduced while surrounded by people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being curtailed' cuts F from SELF to give SEL, which DENY holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Densely means thickly packed, as people are in a crowd.
